raw_response:
I farm 8 mu, and on my land wheat and maize are one set, so I will run the full 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. I do not start from zero. I start from what worked before and what I see around me in Quzhou. With my well, I will not let wheat go dry, because wheat here eats water in the dry season, and if wheat is weak, the whole year is weak. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because these days the better seed usually pays back if the stand is even. On fertilizer, I will spend where it matters most. I will keep nitrogen a little on the safe side, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a bit of fertilizer money. For wheat I will put more fertilizer and more water than maize, because wheat depends more on irrigation here. For maize, rain helps a lot, but I will still keep one irrigation ready if the field is dry after sowing or before tasseling. I will not make the plan too fancy. On 8 mu, simple and steady is better: rotary tillage for wheat after maize, and no-tillage maize after wheat harvest so I can plant fast and catch the season. If pests come, I will spray when I see real pressure, but for the yearly budget I will count on about three sprays in wheat and two in maize. If the weather is normal and the water comes on time, I will aim around 650 kg per mu for wheat and 720 kg per mu for maize. That is a level I feel I can chase without gambling the whole year.
